problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(0,0),(1,5),(2,3).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{\pi /2}$ by an angle of $\frac{\pi }{2}$ radians about the origin?

- $(-5,1)$
- $(0,-2)$
- $(2,-3)$

feedback.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at  $(-2,-4),(1,2),(2,-1).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the **clockwise** rotation ${R}_{-3\pi /2}$ by an angle of $\frac{3\pi }{2}$ radians about the origin?

- $(2,1)$
- $(4,-2)$
- $(-1,2)$
feedback.worked_solution:
The clockwise rotation ${R}_{-3\pi /2}$ by an angle of $\frac{3\pi }{2}$ radians is the same as counterclockwise rotation by an angle of $\frac{\pi }{2}.$ It's given by the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{-3\pi /2},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 2 \\ -4 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{-3\pi /2}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 2 \\ -4 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(4,-2),(-2,1),(1,2).$

So, the correct answer is "II only."
